docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text: The Dashboard is the first page you see after you sign in. It shows where your products and projects stand, and gets you to your next task quickly.

docs.title: Summary chips
docs.text:
The chips at the top show the state of your company's products at a glance.

Chip What it shows Active Projects Projects being worked on now in your organization Pending Tasks Tasks waiting to be done in the system Products in Vault Products in the Product Vault Total Assets (Forms and Manuals) Forms and manuals locked and available in the products in the Vault

docs.text: Recent Activity is a feed of everything happening across your projects and products. Scan it to get up to speed on your organization quickly.

docs.title: Common tasks
docs.text:
• Start a project: select New Project in Quick Actions. To update a product, it must be published in the Vault first; see Review and publish.
  • Import a product: select Import Product in Quick Actions, then follow Create a product and Import documents.
  • Check your tasks: look at Your Tasks, or select View All for the full list.

docs.title: Product Vault overview
docs.text: The Product Vault (the Vault) stores all your existing products in one place, so you can take a quick look at any of them. It is the single source of truth for your forms, rules, rates and supporting documents.

docs.title: Summary chips
docs.text:
The chips at the top of the Vault show:

  • Products: how many products are in the Vault
  • Jurisdictions: how many jurisdictions (states) they cover
  • Lines of business: how many lines they span
  • Last updated: when the Vault last changed

docs.title: Browse your products
docs.text:
You can view products as cards or as a list. TODO verify the view toggle's label and location.

View Shows Card view Each product as a card with its state count and last updated date List view The same information as a table

Open a product to see its jurisdictions.

docs.title: What a product contains
docs.text:
A product is made of:

Asset Tab Forms Forms Manuals Manuals Rules, from your manuals Rules Supporting documents Supporting Materials

Manuals are split into rules and rate tables. When you import files, each one lands in the matching tab.

After import, background processing reads your manuals and structures them into rates and rules. See Process documents.

Products you import become the Baseline: the current version that later updates build on. See Review and publish.

docs.title: Import a product
docs.text:
Choose the way that fits your work:

  • One jurisdiction at a time: build the baseline state by state. Start with Create a product, then Import documents for each jurisdiction.
  • Many jurisdictions at once: use the inventory to populate the whole product from one view. TODO verify where the inventory is and how to open it.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: A few one-time setup steps make creating products in the Vault smooth.

docs.title: Sign in and choose your tenant
docs.text:
1. Sign in with your email first, then your password.
  2. Open the user menu (your initials) and confirm the organization shown, for example Organization — {tenant}.
  3. To change tenant, choose Switch Tenant and select the tenant you want, then Confirm.

Use a test tenant for practice

Try new steps in a test tenant first. Administrators viewing another tenant see a yellow banner with Switch Back.

docs.title: Set up Group and Underwriting Company
docs.text:
Every product needs a Group and an Underwriting Company. Underwriting Company depends on Group, so each company must sit under a group.

  1. Go to System Administration → Lists.
  2. Create the Group value first.
  3. Open Underwriting Company and choose the Grouped by Group view.
  4. Select + Add value under {Group} and enter the company name.
  5. Reload the page and reopen Underwriting Company. The companies should still appear under the group.

Note

If the Underwriting Company field later shows No Options when you create a product, the companies are not linked to a group yet. Repeat the steps above.

docs.title: Check your product list
docs.text: Products are created from your tenant's product list (lines such as Personal and Commercial, and products such as Auto or Homeowners). Make sure the products you need are on the list before you create them. TODO verify where the product list is managed.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Open Product Vault from the left navigation.
  2. Choose Add Existing Product. You can also start from Import Product on the Dashboard. TODO verify button labels.
  3. Choose the line and product, for example Personal → Auto.
  4. Enter the product name.
  5. Select the Group and a linked Underwriting Company.
  6. Select every state (jurisdiction) the product needs.
  7. Save the product, then open it and confirm the states appear.

Choose states carefully

Add all states when you create the product and double-check them before you save (for example AK, not AZ). A way to add a state to an existing product has not been documented yet. TODO verify

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Line Product States Personal Auto AK, AL Personal Homeowners AK, AL Commercial Motor Truck Cargo AK, AL

Next: Import documents.

docs.title: Import documents
docs.text: You upload documents for one jurisdiction at a time. There is no product-level upload.

docs.title: Prepare your files
docs.text:
A simple folder layout keeps imports fast:

{Product}/{State}/Forms/                 .doc or .docx files
{Product}/{State}/Manuals/
{Product}/{State}/Supporting Documents/  goes to the Supporting Materials tab

docs.title: Upload for a state
docs.text:
1. Open the product in the Product Vault and select the jurisdiction.
  2. Open the upload or import view for that jurisdiction. TODO verify button label.
  3. On Forms, use Bulk Import and choose the folder of .doc or .docx forms for that state.
  4. On Manuals, upload the manuals for that state.
  5. On Supporting Materials, upload the supporting documents for that state.
  6. Let each upload finish before you move to the next tab or state.

Suggested order: finish one state completely (Forms → Manuals → Supporting Materials), then move to the next.

docs.title: Check the counts
docs.text:
An upload is complete when the counts in each tab match your files. For example:

Product State Forms Manuals Supporting Materials Auto AK 2 4 2 Auto AL 2 4 2 Homeowners AK 2 5 2 Homeowners AL 2 5 2

After upload the jurisdiction shows Pending Import. That is expected: the next step is Process documents.

docs.title: Process documents
docs.text: Processing turns uploaded files into Vault assets. It needs a little metadata first.

docs.title: 1. Add form metadata
docs.text:
1. Open the jurisdiction → Forms.
  2. Open a row's metadata dialog.
  3. Enter Form Number and Edition. These are the only required fields.
  4. Close the dialog. Closing saves your changes.

Form file names usually follow {PREFIX} {NNNN} {MM} {YY} {Title}.docx:

File name starts with Form Number Edition PPA 0001 07 16 PPA 0001 07 16 HO 0003 09 20 HO 0003 09 20

docs.title: 2. Add manual editions
docs.text:
1. Open Manuals.
  2. For each row, select Edit, enter the Edition, then Save Metadata.
File name clue Edition 01 21, Rev 06 21 01 21, 06 21 Four digits at the end, such as 0823 08 23

docs.title: 3. Process
docs.text:
1. Select Process Documents once.
  2. The status moves to Processing, then Processed. This can take a minute or two. Refresh the page to see the update.
  3. When processing is done, you see Rater and Review & Publish.

Tip

Select Process Documents only once and give it time to finish.

Next: Review and publish.

docs.title: Review and publish
docs.text: Publishing makes a processed jurisdiction the current baseline in the Vault. Your team needs a published product before they can update it in the Project Workbench.

docs.title: 1. Check rules
docs.text: Rules are pulled from your manuals. Open Rules and expand the tree, for example 1 MANUAL FORMAT → 1.1 Multistate Rules Manual. Make sure numbering is complete. If something is missing, check the manual editions on the Manuals tab.

docs.title: 2. Publish
docs.text:
1. Select Review & Publish.
  2. Review the counts. Information Pending should be 0 for Manuals, Forms and Supporting Materials.
  3. Choose the Type of Insurance, for example 19.0 Personal Auto.
  4. Check each Subtype of Insurance that applies.
  5. Set the Effective Date.
  6. Select Publish.
  7. Confirm the release shows as Baseline under Product Resources. TODO verify exact label.

Repeat for each jurisdiction you want to publish.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text: Start a Product Update in the Workbench: Workbench → + New Project → Product Update. TODO verify once the Workbench pages are written.

docs.title: Product import
docs.text:
Audience: External

Bringing a product into the Product Vault (the Vault) takes four simple steps. You can do it in one sitting.

  1. Create the product.
  2. Upload files for each state.
  3. Process and extract rules.
  4. Review and publish your first release. TODO verify

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Have your files ready for each state, in three groups:

Group File types Forms Word or PDF Manuals Word or Excel Supporting documents PDF

One-time setup

Your Group and Underwriting Company should already exist in System Administration → Lists. See Before you start.

docs.title: Create the product
docs.text:
Audience: External

  1. Open Product Vault and choose Add product.
  2. Enter a Product name.
  3. Enter a Description.
  4. Choose an Insurance type: Personal or Commercial.
  5. Choose the Lines of business.
  6. Choose your Group.
  7. Choose your Underwriting company.
  8. Select every state you need under Jurisdictions.
  9. Choose Add product.

You see Product created successfully, and the product status shows Pending Import. Nice work!

docs.title: Lines of business
docs.text:
Insurance type Lines of business Personal Homeowners, Auto, Dwelling Property, Homeowners By Peril Commercial Builders Risk, Motor Truck Cargo, Inland Marine, Commercial Output

Next: Upload files for each state.

docs.title: Process and extract rules
docs.text: Audience: External

docs.title: Configure rules
docs.text:
This tells the Vault how to find rules in your manuals.

  1. Open the Manual tab and choose Configure rules.
  2. On a manual marked Needs configuration, choose Configure.
  3. Choose Configure manually. You can also choose Configure using Word plugin.
  4. Pick the Numbering style that matches your manual's headings, for example multi-level numbers with dots (1, 1.1, 1.1.2).
  5. Optionally, set the font family, size and bold.
  6. Optionally, apply the same setup to your other Word manuals.
  7. Choose Save, then Done.

For Excel manuals, select the rule areas in Excel. A manual marked Shared · 2 is used by more than one state, so you configure it just once.

Configure first, then process

Set up rules before you process. Once a manual is processed, its configuration is locked in.

docs.title: Process documents
docs.text:
1. Choose Process documents.
  2. If a manual isn't configured yet, you'll be asked about it. Choose Continue, or cancel and configure it first.
  3. Wait for processing to finish. Uploads and edits pause while it runs.

When it's done, the status shows {State} · Processed, and the Rules tab lists your extracted rules. The sample Auto and Homeowners manuals produced about 150–180 rules each.

Repeat these steps for each state.

docs.title: Next: review and publish
docs.text: Choose Review & publish to create the state's first release. TODO verify

docs.title: Upload files for each state
docs.text:
Audience: External

You upload files one state at a time.

docs.title: Upload your files
docs.text:
1. Open your product in the Vault.
  2. Choose a state from the Jurisdiction selector.
  3. Open the Forms tab and choose Browse files, or drag and drop. Forms accept DOC, DOCX or PDF.
  4. Open the Manual tab and upload your manuals. Manuals accept PDF, DOC, DOCX, XLS or XLSX.
  5. Open the Supporting Materials tab and upload your supporting documents.

Quick tips

Uploading one file at a time is the most reliable. If a tab count still shows 0 after an upload, refresh the page.

docs.title: Add metadata
docs.text:
New files show Draft, and some show Metadata incomplete until you add their details.

  1. Choose the pencil icon on a file.
  2. For a form, enter the Form number (for example, HO 0003) and the Edition.
  3. Choose Save metadata.

Next: Process and extract rules.
